subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 1: New Media – Project: Design a Blog
outcomes: Know the parts of a blog: homepage, menu, blog post and comments.
Sort blogging tips into Content, Design and Technical.
Plan, build and present a blog with my team and give polite feedback.

tf.s: Someone who writes a blog is a blogger.
tf.why: Yes! A blogger writes blog posts.

tf.s: The blog post page shows the menu and all recent posts.
tf.why: That is the homepage; the post page shows one post with its comments.

tf.s: A menu helps readers move between pages.
tf.why: Correct, it is like a map of the blog.

tf.s: 'Choose attractive colours' is a Design tip.
tf.why: Colours are part of how the blog looks.
It is a Content tip: it is about what and how often you post.

tf.s: Bloggers should post their personal details to make friends.
tf.why: Don't post personal details, to protect your privacy and stay safe.

tf.s: The homepage is the first page of a blog.
tf.why: Well done, readers see it first.

tf.s: In the group, the designer is responsible for the look of the blog.
tf.why: Right, the designer takes care of the creative side.

tf.s: 'Your blog is bad' is a polite way to give feedback.
tf.why: Try: 'Your blog is good, but you could add more photos.'

tf.s: Feedback from another group cannot help us improve.
tf.why: Others can see points we cannot see ourselves.

boxes.q: Someone who writes a blog is a ...
boxes.why: A blogger writes and posts on a blog.
Colours are about the look of the blog.
It is about posting content often.

boxes.q: Which feature helps readers move between pages?
boxes.why: The menu links the pages together.

boxes.q: What does the blog post page show?
boxes.why: Each post has its own page with comments.

boxes.q: Why shouldn't you post personal details?
Which word means 'the way things are arranged on a page'?
boxes.why: Layout is how the parts of a page are placed.

o: Why don't we blog about technology?

boxes.q: Today our group will ___ our blog to the class.
boxes.why: We present our work to classmates.

boxes.q: Which question helps you reflect on teamwork?
o: How well did you work together as a team?
boxes.why: Reflection questions help you think about your work.

hunt.q: A person who writes a blog
The first page of a blog
Team member who makes the look
Show your blog to the class

mcq.q: What does a blog homepage show?
mcq.why: The homepage gives an overview of the blog.

mcq.q: What are the three categories of blogging tips?
mcq.why: Noora's tips are sorted into these three groups.

mcq.q: What is the designer's role in the group?
o: the creative side and the look of the blog
mcq.why: The designer makes the blog look good.

mcq.q: Which word means 'what is written and shown on the blog'?
mcq.why: Content is the information in your posts.

mcq.q: Your group wants to suggest a topic. What do you say?
o: Why don't we blog about robots and technology?
mcq.why: 'Why don't we…?' is a clear suggestion.

o: Your blog is good, but you could add more photos.
mcq.why: Polite feedback gives a positive point and a suggestion.

mcq.q: Which two things does a good presentation need?
o: a clear voice and good timing
a quiet voice and no eye contact
reading very fast and no plan
mcq.why: A clear voice, eye contact and good timing help listeners.

mcq.q: Why is 'Don't post personal details' an important tip?
o: It protects your privacy and keeps you safe.
It makes the blog more colourful.
mcq.why: Personal details online can be unsafe.

mcq.q: Why is feedback from another group useful?
o: It shows points to improve that we cannot see ourselves.
It means we don't need to plan.
mcq.why: Fresh eyes help raise the quality of our work.

mcq.q: A blog has many posts but readers can't find the pages. What should the group add?
mcq.why: A menu helps readers move between pages.
